description: A timeline comparison of how Meta’s Facebook/Instagram feed dominance surged as short-form video and creator ecosystems exploded—while Twitter/X stumbled through ownership shocks, ad-market turbulence, and engagement volatility.
youtube_description:
📈 In this chart-race timeline, we track the social-media feed power shift: Meta’s Facebook + Instagram feeds vs Twitter/X’s turbulence as TikTok’s short-form era detonates.

00:00 — The early feed era (2011–2014): Facebook scales steadily; Instagram is still ramping.
02:10 — 2015–2016: Instagram becomes an attention magnet; TikTok begins its breakout ramp.
04:20 — 2017–2018: Meta’s engagement flywheel tightens while Twitter’s growth flattens.
06:40 — 2019–2020: TikTok goes mainstream; Facebook remains an MAU monster; Twitter begins to slide.
08:50 — 2021–2022: The short-form/feed battle sharpens—Instagram accelerates; Twitter churns.
11:10 — 2023–2025: TikTok stabilizes into a top-tier attention platform; Facebook + Instagram stay massive; X fights for consistency.

🎬 Video goal: a high-contrast “feed takeover” story—one player rises while another gets crushed.

✅ If you want more chart-race datasets like this, SUBSCRIBE and drop a comment: which platform do you think wins the next 5 years—Facebook/Instagram, TikTok, or X?

Sources: company investor materials and widely reported MAU figures for major platforms (e.g., Meta quarterly disclosures and reputable industry reporting consolidations).
instagram_caption:
🚀 The Social Feed Takeover: how Meta’s feed won—while X lost the plot.

Picture 2011: Facebook is already a global default. Then Instagram starts quietly building the “scroll” habit that would later define modern social. In 2011, Facebook sits at ~905M monthly active users (MAU). By 2014 it’s ~1.24B—steady, unbothered, and feeding an ever-growing network effect.

But the real chaos starts when Instagram and short-form video begin reshaping attention. Instagram goes from ~250M MAU in 2014 to ~700M by 2017, and by 2020 it hits ~1.2B. Meanwhile TikTok, starting from ~0 in the early years, explodes into the top-tier conversation—reaching ~1.0B MAU by 2020 and ~1.65B by 2025.

Then watch the contrast: Twitter/X. Through 2016–2017 it still hovers around ~485–490M. By 2018 it drops to ~430M, and 2019 slides to ~330M. Even in the 2020s, as TikTok and Meta dominate new attention cycles, X never fully rebounds—tracking ~300M–320M MAU through 2023–2025.

This is why the chart-race hits hard: Meta isn’t just growing—it’s compounding. Facebook rises from ~2.13B MAU in 2019 to ~3.2B by 2025, while Instagram keeps climbing to ~1.95B. TikTok becomes the new disruptor. And X becomes the cautionary tale: when engagement shifts, the platform that doesn’t adapt gets squeezed.

👇 Question for you: do you think the “feed takeover” belongs to Meta forever, or will TikTok permanently steal the center of gravity?
